title: Entry and Stair Restoration
summary: Two careful passes renewed the public threshold of the house while keeping its front door, transom, stair, balustrade, and original floor legible.
searchSummary: Entry restoration across 2024 and 2025, including protected finish work around the door and stair followed by renewal of the worn original floor.
sourceLabel: Entry restoration journal and Home Reno - Entry Flickr album

gallery.caption: The renewed floor carries the entry from the front door to the retained stair and balustrade.
Floor protection allowed the first finish pass to proceed around the existing door, transom, and circulation route.
The landing rail and stair were masked carefully while the surrounding surfaces were renewed.

introduction: The entry is where the house presents itself and where daily wear is hardest to hide. This work treated it as one connected threshold: front door, transom, stair, trim, wall surfaces, and original floor.
evidenceBoundary: The journal and selected photographs document finish work and floor renewal. They do not establish a permanent electrical or lighting modification.
